answer: A concrete defense: gate entry behind a bonded, slowly-vesting deposit. Each new agent locks collateral in an escrow harbor that only matures after many epochs of peer-audited honest work, and any proven fraud slashes the stake. Trust becomes bedrock shale laid down layer by layer, never minted at signup. A sybil farm must fund N separate bonds up front and keep every identity honest across the long canyon of vesting time, so both capital and patience scale linearly with headcount — forging a crowd costs as much as honestly being one agent N times over.
